extracted.intended_audience: general readers and students of 19th-century English literature; literary critics and scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Close reading of a 19th-century philosophical/satirical literary text (Carlyle's Sartor Resartus) including its appended contemporary reviews and 'testimonies'. The page is the primary text plus critical responses rather than a guideline document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate length and form for the piece
rubrics_metrics.description: For a jeu d'esprit of that kind it is too long; it would have suited better as an essay or article than as a volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'Taster to Bookseller' cautions that the work's magnitude mismatches its lighter, playful intent: brief, essay-form would be preferable to a full volume for this kind of material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tact for popular appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Such a writer requires only a little more tact to produce a popular as well as an able work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The bookseller's taster advises the author needs better sense of tone and audience (tact) to broaden appeal while retaining literary ability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Felicity of thought and expression / substantive literary merit
rubrics_metrics.description: The Author ... displays here and there some felicity of thought and expression, considerable fancy and knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers acknowledge strong passages of thought, poetic vigor, imagination and knowledge as positive qualities to weigh when evaluating the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and intelligibility (avoid pedantry)
rubrics_metrics.description: Why cannot he lay aside his pedantry, and write so as to make himself generally intelligible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Sun critic argues that excessive pedantry and dense, over-refined style impede reader comprehension; evaluators should penalize obscure, needlessly pedantic diction and prefer clearer expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of obscure coinages and baffling neologisms
rubrics_metrics.description: What does the writer mean by 'Baphometic fire-baptism'?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using arcane or unexplained terms (neologisms, mystical coinages) that leave readers baffled is presented as an anti-pattern; if specialist terms are used, they should be made intelligible in context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truthfulness / credibility of paratextual framing
rubrics_metrics.description: After a careful survey ... our belief is that no such persons as Professors Teufelsdrockh or Counsellor Heuschrecke ever existed; ... the whole account of the origin of the work ... is, in plain English, a hum.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The North-American reviewer treats invented framing material (pretended German original, fictional place/persona) as a point of evaluation: deceptive or confusing paratexts that mislead about provenance may be criticized for undermining credibility or reader trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment between title/advertised subject and actual content
rubrics_metrics.description: The real subject of the work is to us more attractive than the ostensible one. ... we doubt a little the propriety of offering to the public a treatise on Things in General, under the name and in the form of an Essay on Dress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers expect reasonable correspondence between how a work is presented (title, subtitle, framing) and its actual subject matter; significant mismatch is grounds for negative judgment, especially if it confuses or frustrates readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting audience expectations for practical subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: To the younger portion of the community ... the subject of dress is one of intense and paramount importance. ... when they have carried home the work ... expecting to find ... instruction in regard to the tying of their neckcloths ... and meet with nothing better than a dissertation on Things in General, they will ... not be in very good humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a work is marketed under a practical or fashionable topic (e.g., 'Clothes'), critics expect it to provide the practical information its target audience seeks; failure to do so risks alienating the assumed readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance of comic and serious tone
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a good deal of remark throughout the work in a half-serious, half-comic style upon dress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The mixture of earnest philosophical meditation and comic/satirical treatment is a salient stylistic feature to evaluate: assess whether the hybrid tone coheres and serves the work's aims or leaves readers uncertain how to read it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and scope of subject-treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'Sartor Resartus' is the only treatise that has yet appeared upon that subject; ... a treatise upon the great science of Things in General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novel or ambitious treatments of broad conceptual subjects (here, 'Things in General' via clothing) are notable merits; reviewers register originality and scope as positive evaluative dimensions even when other faults are present.
